summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, with hands-on embedded firmware experience on ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers. Built bare-metal C and FreeRTOS firmware driving SPI, I2C, and UART peripherals, PWM motor control, and closed-loop sensor feedback for robotic and embedded hardware. Debugged firmware, hardware, and mechanism failures at the bench with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers during hardware bring-up, and designed and fabricated the PCBs the firmware ran on.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth (BLE/Classic) to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and firmware integration end-to-end.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM motor control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override on STM32.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization for closed-loop feedback.
Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Built Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) by isolating faults across firmware, hardware, and mechanism; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via TCA9548A I2C mux.
Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection.
